views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep the May 19 cease-fire and send Ross to lock specifics, but do not treat a purchase pledge as the deal. Convert China’s vague promise to “significantly increase” US goods and services into time-bound agriculture and energy volumes while keeping the Section 301 list and the ZTE denial order in reserve until there is enforceable movement on forced tech transfer, cyber theft, and IP. Do not escalate tariffs this week—talks are live and the US economy is not yet paying a tariff bill—and do not trade ZTE relief for a deficit photo-op.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is a modest US opportunity, not a crisis. The 301 report (2018-03-22) established a real structural problem, and China’s proposed $50B soy/auto/aircraft list (2018-04-04) plus the April $3B 232 retaliation show farm-belt and export exposure if talks collapse. But the current state of the dispute favors Washington: Section 301 duties are still only proposed (USTR hearings 15–17 May; rebuttals through 22 May), the ZTE denial order (2018-04-16) has already halted ZTE’s main operations, and the 19 May joint statement plus Mnuchin’s “trade war on hold” line show Beijing bidding purchases rather than matching a tariff cascade. US macro is not biting: UMCSENT 98, INDPRO ~102, VIX 12.58 on 23 May, goods deficit narrower at -$66.6B; China IP is still ~6.8% y/y and the yuan is firmer than late 2017. That is closer to leverage than to GDP drag. Action should stay at negotiate, not escalate or concede. Escalating now would invite the soy/auto hit before structural talks have a chance and would contradict a pause we just announced. Conceding—especially a ZTE walk-back after Trump’s 13 May tweet, which a House panel already moved to block—would spend the strongest chip for what Lighthizer correctly called a secondary issue. Nov 2017 already showed China will sign commercial MOUs without IP concessions. Hold the tools, make Ross extract hard purchase schedules, and keep structural change as the price of any lasting tariff or ZTE relief.
key_factors: May 19 joint statement is purchases-only; no dollar figure and no IP/tech-transfer text
ZTE denial order remains the strongest live US chip; Congress is blocking a cheap pardon
Section 301 $50B list and China soy/auto/aircraft list are proposed, not in force
US real economy and risk markets are calm; dispute is not yet a GDP event
Lighthizer: structural IP/cyber > deficit math; tariffs stay in reserve

sources_cited.excerpt: US and China release joint statement after talks: China agrees to "significantly increase" purchases of US goods and services. Mnuchin says trade war is "on hold." Markets rally.
US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.

USTR releases Section 301 report finding China's IP/tech-transfer practices unreasonable or discriminatory. Trump signs presidential memorandum directing tariffs on Chinese imports, a WTO case, and investment restrictions.
China announces proposed retaliatory tariffs on ~$50B of US goods (including soybeans, automobiles, and aircraft) in response to the Section 301 list.
USTR publishes proposed Section 301 tariff list: ~1,300 Chinese product lines (~$50B), targeting aerospace, ICT, robotics, machinery and related sectors.
Trump visits Beijing; large package of commercial deals announced (many MOUs). No substantive concessions on structural IP / tech-transfer issues.
University of Michigan consumer sentiment latest 98 (2018-05-01); still elevated, no trade-war collapse in household confidence.
VIX 12.58 on 2018-05-23 after the May 19 pause; far below the March 23 spike (24.87) around the 301 memorandum.
US goods trade deficit -$66.6B (2018-05-01), narrower than Dec 2017; dispute not widening the headline gap yet.
US industrial production 102.4 (2018-05-01); activity still expanding, no tariff-cascade hit in the data.

Lighthizer: opening China to more US exports is significant, but forced technology transfers, cyber theft, and protection of innovation are far more important; US may still use tariffs, investment restrictions, and export regulations. Real structural change is necessary.

Mnuchin: planned tariffs on as much as $150B of Chinese goods are off the table while talks proceed. Experts warn suspending tariffs could undercut leverage; ZTE standoff was a significant reason more progress was not made.
House Appropriations Committee unanimously added language upholding ZTE sanctions days after Trump tweeted Commerce should get ZTE 'back into business, fast.'
